To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

imatinib (a tyrosine kinase inhibitor used to treat CML) induces centrosomal amplifications in BCR- ABL-positive cells and that this induction is mediated by increased proteolytic activity (catalytic activity) of the protease Separase.

(1) Separase, an enzyme that triggers the separation of sister chromatids, is overexpressed in cancer, (2) Separase is frequently over-expressed in chronic myeloid leukaemia (CML), (3) Separase activity is increased by the CML oncogene p210BCRABL and (4) Separase activity can be further increased by the CMI drug Imatinib, which may promote the development of resistance in CML
the proteolytic Separase activity in BCR-ABLP-positive cells is increased by IM.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of p210BCRL-ABL and imatinib on the proteolytic Separase activity in CML.
Separase, a potential driver of genomic instability in CML.
the influence of the BCR-ABL tyrosin-kinase on Separase and its proteolytic activity, as well as with the influence of therapeutic doses of imatnib on Separase and Separase proteolytis activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proteolytic Separase activity in CML cells is increased by IM.
IM induces centrosomal alterations, which are more pronounced in p210BC-R-ABL positive cells, but the underlying molecular mechanism is not yet fully understood and needs further investigations.
the p210BCRABL-tyrosine kinase activity is able to increase the proteolytic Separase activity and that imatinib is not able to counteract this effect, but even increases Separase activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Separase is activated in BCR-ABl-positive cells and this may contribute to genomic instability, resistance and clonal evolution.
IM treatment of CML cells increases the proteolytic function of Separase in p210BC-RABl-positive cells, which may contribute to the genomic instability and clonal evolution in CML.
IM induces centrosomal ampliﬁcation in p210BC-ABL-positive cells by activation of the aneuploidity-promoter Separase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
imatinib treatment induces centrosomal amplifications in BCR-ABl-positive CML cells.
the proteolytic function of separase is increased in BCR-ABl-positive cells and that this increase is not counteracted by imatinib.
the proteolytic activation of Separase by BCR-ABL is an important mechanism for centrosome amplification and genomic stability in CML, which is counteracted by imatinib.
